newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Israel grilled at UN on torture of Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel grilled at UN on torture of Palestinians.

text.p: Israel was asked at a U.N. forum on Wednesday to explain its use of torture against Palestinians including shaking and sleep deprivation.

Bent Sorensen, a member of the U.N. Committee against Torture, said methods used by the Jewish state included constant interrogation over long periods, violent shaking, and cutting circulation with tight handcuffs.
Awkward and painful sitting positions and refusal to use the toilet were also used, he told a meeting of the commission.
Sorensen, a medical doctor, spoke of an autopsy report of one victim who died after an Israeli interrogation. He said the report established that violent shaking was the cause of death.
"We have medical proof this is torture," he said. "All cases of shaking can only be considered as torture from a medical point of view."
The Danish expert, referring to Denmark's wartime help to the suffering Jews, added: "It is really unbearable to myself that this nation and only this nation allows torture."

Israel's justice ministry director-general Nili Arad defended her country's interrogation methods as lawful and denied that torture existed in Israel, but conceded that some methods used were "unpleasant."

"In interrogations whose subject is the prevention of acts of terrorism, investigators are permitted in certain exceptional cases to use methods which would normally be regarded as unacceptable in regular interrogations," she said.

"While we realise that these methods are unpleasant, none of them come anywhere near what would constitute torture under U.N. conventions," she told the 10-member commission, which opened its semi-annual meeting in Geneva this month to monitor states' compliance with the 1987 Convention against Torture.
